category_state.finding: No active Information Theory items exist yet. Literature sources establish the external statement interfaces only; proposed library items need local proofs or proved local suppliers.

published_suppliers.supports: Markov-kernel vocabulary and composition, construction/uniqueness of sequential laws, and explicit probability models for discrete-time channel sequences. Reuse the kernel definitions only after checking the channel’s alphabets and measurability assumptions.

Stationary/memoryless process-law existence and uniqueness from consistent finite-dimensional distributions on the stated standard-Borel coordinate spaces. Does not itself prove a coding theorem or disintegration theorem for arbitrary spaces.
Standard-Borel measurability and determining-class foundations where a general-alphabet one-shot statement uses them. Preserve the page’s stated choice assumptions.

The iid information-density convergence in the direct part of the stationary-memoryless Shannon theorem, provided the information density is integrable (finite mutual information). Also supports iid cost typicality when the cost is integrable.

Qualitative normal approximation/convergence-in-law interface under the page’s moment and array hypotheses. The page expressly supplies no quantitative Berry–Esseen remainder; it cannot prove the O(log n) finite-blocklength term.

Likelihood ratios and information densities when absolute continuity and the source theorem’s sigma-finiteness/finite-measure hypotheses hold. Singular parts must be kept explicit rather than silently replaced by densities.
Product-channel calculations and exchanging integrals/sums only under the stated sigma-finiteness, nonnegative, or L1 hypotheses.
Jensen/limit-exchange steps in cost-capacity and information arguments under each result’s stated integrability and measure assumptions.

Simple-vs-simple testing reductions in hypothesis-testing converses, including randomized threshold treatment and the source’s common sigma-finite dominating measure/singular-mass premises. It does not define or prove every quantum or composite testing analogue.
Finite-dimensional simplex concavity/Jensen steps in DMC capacity and power allocation.
Finite-dimensional convexity and supporting-hyperplane interfaces. Check relative-interior and lower-semicontinuity conditions at each use.
Compactness/attainment arguments on finite probability simplices and finite-dimensional feasible polytopes; these do not transfer automatically to infinite-dimensional alphabets.
Convex separation interfaces for variational and minimax arguments when the topological closure and choice assumptions match.
Weak-topology/convex-closure facts only; no channel theorem follows without the required compactness and continuity proof.
Weak-star compactness and extreme-point interfaces for advanced variational arguments; all topology, duality, and choice premises remain explicit.
Finite-dimensional Gaussian covariance diagonalization and matrix square roots where the item’s real/complex and positive-semidefinite hypotheses apply.
Some finite-sample tail estimates under their own boundedness/sub-Gaussian hypotheses; does not supply a Berry–Esseen theorem or general DMC reliability function.

draft_or_unavailable_suppliers.use_status: Do not count as published proof suppliers. The finite-alphabet parallel-AWGN power-allocation proof may instead give a local elementary concavity/KKT derivation with all active-set and endpoint cases.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: No published IT definitions/items: entropy, KL/f-divergence, mutual information, information density, coding, capacity, cost-constrained code, feedback code, one-shot testing parameter, error exponent, or Blahut–Arimoto. The Information Theory category is draft and empty.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: Build definitions with measurable alphabets/kernels, log/support/extended-real conventions, units, and error/cost model; prove every new result locally or link to adequate proved items. Coordinate information-measure supplier interfaces with r1.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: No published Berry–Esseen or other quantitative normal-approximation theorem. Existing CLTs prove convergence in law only.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: Add/prove a quantitative normal approximation with explicit moment and constant hypotheses, and combine it with one-shot coding/converse bounds and the corrected local quadratic-decay argument before claiming the O(log n) remainder.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: The published Neyman–Pearson lemma is a simple-testing supplier, not the full channel meta-converse, composite minimax interchange, or strong-converse proof.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: Define beta/test conventions and prove the channel-code-to-test reduction, auxiliary-output choice, and asymptotic testing limit under the exact finite-alphabet or integrability assumptions.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: No published BA correctness/convergence or numerical-complexity item. The optimization/KKT page is draft; PW refers elsewhere for convergence proof.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: State finite alphabet and initialization/support/output conventions; prove each iterate and the lower/upper bounds are well-defined, monotone, and converge to capacity; relate the exact-arithmetic gap test to eventual tolerance termination and give a finite-n gap/resource guarantee if one is claimed. Specify floating-point/error/resource model separately; asymptotic convergence alone gives no certified finite-resource bound.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: No existing library supplier for Shannon/Feinstein random coding, packing/converse, expurgation, Fano, error exponents, or the constrained-code extension.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: Supply finite-block code construction and converse arguments, including random-code averaging/selection and every distinction between average and maximal error, per-codeword and expected cost.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: Kernel/Radon–Nikodym/probability foundations exist, but this lane found no single published package proving the needed disintegration, entropy maximization, information stability, Gaussian-process spectral calculus, or continuous-time channel coding results under complete hypotheses.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: Restrict initial theorems to finite or standard-Borel alphabets where premises can be verified. Treat PW’s continuous-time AWGN discussion as a sketch until operator/spectral and coding arguments are supplied.

missing_local_suppliers.missing: The exact low-rate DMC reliability function is an open problem in the source, not a missing local proof of a known theorem.
missing_local_suppliers.required_local_work: If included, state proved upper/lower bounds as bounds; record the exact equality question separately as an open problem, never as a supplier.
